lede.headline: Zuckerberg turns his AI agent into a toll booth
lede.dek: At Meta Connect, Zuckerberg said the Muse AI agent will stay free but eventually earn Meta a small fee on the purchases, bookings and bills it completes, with Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora and Wayfair among the retailers signing on.

top10AsOf: Net worths per Forbes' "The Top 10 Richest People In The World," September 2026 update (based on the Sept 1, 2026 snapshot). Forbes and Bloomberg Billionaires Index coverage this week shows no change to the order as of Sept 24-25, 2026.

stories.headline: Zuckerberg turns Meta's AI agent into a toll booth
stories.move: At Meta Connect's Sept. 23-24 sessions, Zuckerberg said Muse, Meta's AI agent, will stay free for a large number of tokens, then earn Meta a small fee on transactions it completes. Meta added PayPal support and shopping integrations with Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Wayfair and American Eagle, plus travel booking through Expedia and grocery orders via Instacart.
stories.why: Meta is betting that owning the AI agent people shop through is worth more than ad revenue alone. The fee comes from merchants, not users, so wider Muse adoption compounds directly into Meta's revenue.
stories.bear: The model depends on people trusting an AI agent to spend money on their behalf, and Meta hasn't said what the fee will be or when it starts.
stories.watch: How many retailers and users actually adopt Muse checkout once it leaves the keynote stage.

stories.headline: Trump and Xi meet, but Nvidia's China question stays open
stories.move: Trump hosted Xi Jinping at the White House on Sept. 24. AI safety cooperation came up in the talks, but chip export controls remained a sticking point and neither side signaled it would slow the AI race.
stories.why: Nvidia's own guidance already assumes zero data-center chip sales to China, so any real opening would be pure upside. The summit didn't deliver one.
stories.bear: Even where Washington has approved chip export licenses for Chinese firms, Beijing has reportedly discouraged its own companies from taking delivery, so a policy win in Washington may not translate into actual sales.
stories.watch: Any follow-up announcement on chip licensing after this week's talks.

stories.headline: Arnault family rebuilds LVMH's holding company to lock in control
stories.move: The Arnault family plans to fold its LVMH stake into Christian Dior SE, then rename that entity Agache SCA, replacing Christian Dior as the family's single listed holding vehicle over LVMH.
stories.why: A simpler structure makes it easier to keep LVMH under family control across generations, at a time when Arnault has not named a single successor among his five children.
stories.bear: Restructuring family control doesn't fix LVMH's underlying problem: luxury demand has been soft enough this year that Arnault fell out of the world's top 10 richest.
stories.watch: Whether the restructuring comes with any signal on succession.

stories.headline: Berkshire builds a nearly 10% stake in homebuilder Lennar
stories.move: Berkshire Hathaway bought 2.67 million Lennar Class A shares and 75,021 Class B shares between Sept. 17 and Sept. 21, worth about $212.4 million, taking its total position to nearly 10% of Lennar and about $1.8 billion. The buying started a day after Lennar missed third-quarter earnings estimates.
stories.why: It's Berkshire's second housing bet under CEO Greg Abel, after it agreed to buy homebuilder Taylor Morrison for about $6.8 billion in a deal that closed in July.
stories.bear: Lennar's stock fell on the earnings miss that preceded Berkshire's buying, and homebuilders are still working through weak demand and high mortgage rates.
stories.watch: Whether Berkshire keeps adding to the Lennar stake, and Lennar's next earnings report.

stories.headline: Adani pledges over ₹1 lakh crore for West Bengal by 2035
stories.move: Gautam Adani said his group will invest more than ₹1 lakh crore in West Bengal by 2035, covering ports, logistics, renewable energy, power, roads, green cement and hyperscale data centers. He also laid the foundation for a 2,000-bed hospital in Kolkata, part of a separate ₹4,000 crore healthcare investment.
stories.why: The announcement came a day after the Hurun India Rich List put Adani back ahead of Mukesh Ambani as India's richest person.
stories.bear: Pledges over a decade-long horizon are easy to announce; how much becomes signed contracts depends on approvals and market conditions that can shift many times before 2035.
stories.watch: How much of the pledge turns into signed contracts and groundbreakings over the next year.

stories.headline: Paramount's Warner Bros. Discovery deal risks a daily penalty
stories.move: Paramount Skydance's $31-per-share cash deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery must close by Sept. 30 or Paramount owes WBD shareholders a ticking fee that accrues daily on top of that price. A group called Block the Merger is still fighting the deal in court, with amicus briefs due Sept. 25.
stories.why: Every day past Sept. 30 raises the price Ellison-backed Paramount pays for WBD, on top of the legal costs of fighting off the merger challenge.
stories.bear: The fee is small day to day, and Paramount has already shown it's willing to pay to keep the deal moving rather than let it collapse.
stories.watch: Whether the deal closes by Sept. 30, and the outcome of the Sept. 25 amicus filings.

stories.headline: Investors keep betting on Tesla's robotaxi story, not car sales
stories.move: Tesla shares rallied roughly 6.75% over the past week. Robotaxi service now runs in seven U.S. metros, and active FSD subscriptions have reached 1.48 million, up 56% year over year. Tesla expects 2026 capital spending above $25 billion, rising further as it builds out Robotaxi, Optimus, chips and AI compute.
stories.why: Even after Goldman Sachs cut its delivery estimates for the rest of the year, investors are pricing Tesla on autonomy and robots, not on how many cars it sells.
stories.bear: Federal regulators are still investigating whether Tesla's steering-wheel-free Cybercabs comply with safety rules, and the robotaxi fleet remains small and geofenced to a handful of cities.
stories.watch: The Tesla Roadster unveiling on Oct. 10.

stories.headline: Murdochs weigh reuniting Fox Corp and News Corp
stories.move: Court documents and testimony unsealed this month in a Fox shareholder lawsuit show Rupert and Lachlan Murdoch are weighing recombining Fox Corp and News Corp, 13 years after splitting the TV and publishing businesses apart.
stories.why: A reunited company would tighten the family's grip over both operations at once, echoing an option Rupert Murdoch considered and shelved in 2022 after investor pushback.
stories.bear: That same investor pushback from 2022 hasn't gone away, and a Delaware judge has separately ordered Fox to hand over hundreds of documents in the underlying shareholder case.
stories.watch: Whether the family moves from considering the re-merger to actually proposing one.

stories.headline: Reliance plans a second rupee bond sale this month
stories.move: Reliance Industries is planning to raise up to ₹100 billion (about $1 billion) through AAA-rated, 10-year local-currency bonds, its second such offering in September after an earlier ₹125 billion sale, which was Reliance's first rupee bond deal since 2023.
stories.why: Two bond sales in one month show Reliance leaning on debt markets to fund its energy, telecom, retail and AI data-center buildout rather than relying only on operating cash flow.
stories.bear: Stacking two large bond deals in a single month adds to Reliance's debt load, at a time when the Hurun list shows Ambani's wealth down 10% year over year.
stories.watch: The final pricing and investor demand for the new bond sale.

watch: Sept 25: Deadline for amicus briefs in the "Block the Merger" challenge to the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery deal.
Sept 30: Paramount's ticking fee on the WBD deal begins accruing if the merger hasn't closed.
Oct 10: Tesla unveils the new Roadster.
quickHits: Nvidia's new Vera Rubin AI systems are shipping in the second half of 2026 to CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius.
Prediction market Kalshi could be valued near $42 billion in a future funding round; its two founders are already billionaires on paper, but its CEO has ruled out an IPO before 2027.
Dell Technologies CFO David Kennedy sold about $14 million of shares on Sept. 22, separate from founder Michael Dell's own stake.
memo: AI agents are becoming sales channels: Meta's Muse now takes a cut of purchases through Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora and others. If you sell to consumers, work out how an AI agent would represent your product.
Berkshire is buying into battered housing stocks like Lennar. If your business touches homebuilding, expect well-capitalized buyers to keep hunting for bargains through this downturn.

Founders are locking in control before handing off, from LVMH's new holding structure to the Murdochs weighing a Fox-News Corp remerger. If your business has multiple owners, document governance before a crisis forces the issue.
